title: "Configure a network interface"
description: "Writes a netplan file of the interface's own, such as /etc/netplan/osapi-osapi0.yaml for osapi0, under a netplan definition that is the interface's own, and applies it. type is ethernet, the default, or dummy. An ethernet is an interface the host has, in the netplan section that netplan status gives for it: one the host does not have is not found. A dummy goes under dummy-devices, and netplan apply makes it, so the host need not have it. dummy-devices needs netplan 0.107 or later. dhcp4 and dhcp6 are false unless given, so the interface has only the addresses given. An interface that a match defines, such as cloud-init's all for en*, is refused, because the config would change each interface the match takes, now and later. An interface osapi already configures does not change: update replaces its config. It runs on the Debian family, and elsewhere, and in a container, reports skipped."

Writes a netplan file of the interface's own, such as /etc/netplan/osapi-osapi0.yaml for osapi0, under a netplan definition that is the interface's own, and applies it. type is ethernet, the default, or dummy. An ethernet is an interface the host has, in the netplan section that netplan status gives for it: one the host does not have is not found. A dummy goes under dummy-devices, and netplan apply makes it, so the host need not have it. dummy-devices needs netplan 0.107 or later. dhcp4 and dhcp6 are false unless given, so the interface has only the addresses given. An interface that a match defines, such as cloud-init's all for en*, is refused, because the config would change each interface the match takes, now and later. An interface osapi already configures does not change: update replaces its config. It runs on the Debian family, and elsewhere, and in a container, reports skipped.
